title_en: Where Chinese Exports Are Gaining the Most Market Share
title_zh: 中国出口在哪里抢到了最多市场份额
subtitle_zh: Goldman Sachs 的 Trina Chen 拆解中国企业出海抢份额的真实图景：新兴市场收入增速是当地市场的 15 倍，而“靠便宜取胜”的老印象正在失效。
description: Where Chinese Exports Are Gaining the Most Market Share

turns.en: The U.S.-China Trade Relationship gets most of the attention, but is that where the most consequential competition is taking place? And what does that mean for companies and investors? I'm Allison Nathan and this is Goldman Sachs Exchanges. My guest today, Trina Chen, co-head of Greater China Equity Research at Goldman Sachs, has
turns.zh: 中美贸易关系（U.S.-China trade relationship）吸引了绝大部分关注，但最具决定性的竞争真的发生在那里吗？这又对企业（companies）和投资者（investors）意味着什么？我是 Allison Nathan，这里是 Goldman Sachs Exchanges。今天的嘉宾 Trina Chen 是 Goldman Sachs 大中华区股票研究联席主管（co-head of Greater China Equity Research），她

turns.en: studied 11 sectors and 40 Chinese and global companies to see where Chinese firms are gaining ground. And what that means for competitors and investors. Trina, welcome to the program. Thank you for having me. So Trina, as I just said so much of the conversation around Chinese companies going global centers
turns.zh: 研究了 11 个行业、40 家中国及全球企业，想弄清楚中国企业究竟在哪些地方站稳了脚跟，这对竞争对手和投资者又意味着什么。Trina，欢迎做客我们的节目。谢谢邀请。那么 Trina，正如我刚才说的，围绕中国企业出海（going global）的讨论，很多都聚焦在

turns.en: on the U.S.-China relationship, but you actually did a lot of work and mapped out where Chinese companies are gaining share worldwide. What did the picture look like? And first, tell us a little bit about the analysis you did. We actually looked through over 10 sectors across all the different industries.
turns.zh: 中美关系上。但你们其实做了大量工作，把中国企业在全球各地抢占市场份额（market share）的情况都梳理了出来。这幅图景到底是什么样的？先请你给我们讲讲你们做的这项分析。我们实际上遍查了横跨各个产业的 10 多个行业。

turns.en: So these are very traditional ones, such as white goods, freezing washer, and they could be EV. And all the way it goes to some of the newer sectors, such as the surgical robot, power equipment, to even services sectors, such as express services. And what we found was a pretty clear, consistent picture in share gaining.
turns.zh: 这里面有很传统的领域，比如白色家电（white goods）里的冰箱、洗衣机，也包括电动车（EV）；一路延伸到一些较新的行业，比如手术机器人（surgical robot）、电力设备（power equipment），甚至还有服务业，比如快递服务（express services）。我们发现，抢占份额的图景相当清晰，而且高度一致。

turns.en: But if you look in the details of all these products in the past five to ten years, about half of them actually the export went to emerging markets. And in these markets, the share gain and revenue growth has been very tremendous. And we're looking at aggregated revenue growth is probably 15 times of the local market organic growth.
turns.zh: 但如果细看过去五到十年所有这些产品的情况，其中约有一半的出口其实是流向新兴市场（emerging markets）的。在这些市场里，份额提升和收入增长都非常惊人。我们看到，加总起来的收入增速大概是当地市场内生增速（organic growth）的 15 倍。

turns.en: And this is where market share today of the Chinese product in emerging market has probably reached 24%. And we see very similar trend in U.S. and Europe, but maybe relative modest, and we're looking at 10 to 16% market share achieved in the X-China market by these companies.
turns.zh: 也正因为如此，中国产品今天在新兴市场的份额大概已经达到 24%。在美国和欧洲我们也看到非常类似的趋势，只不过相对温和一些——这些企业在中国以外（ex-China）市场拿到的份额大约在 10% 到 16% 之间。

turns.en: So market share is gaining everywhere for Chinese exports, but most strikingly in the emerging markets. Think about this growth in Chinese exports. We generally think that means falling prices. The data that you're looking at actually back that up. That's where I think we got one of the biggest surprise in the studies when we look at
turns.zh: 所以说，中国出口在各处都在抢占份额，但在新兴市场最为抢眼。而说到中国出口的增长，我们一般会认为那意味着价格下跌。你们看到的数据真的支持这个判断吗？我觉得，这项研究里最大的意外之一恰恰就出在这儿：当我们看着

turns.en: the chart, we say, wow, this looks different. Intuitively, I think we would be all associated with the Chinese product, with price deflation, price cut. But in reality, what the chart actually shows you, at the beginning of the entry, Chinese product typically come to a market with 30% on average discount to the incumbent local
turns.zh: 那张图表时，我们会说：“哇，这看起来不一样。”凭直觉，我想大家都会把中国产品和价格通缩（price deflation）、降价联系在一起。但实际上图表告诉你的是：在进入市场的初期，中国产品通常以比当地在位同行（incumbent local peers）平均低 30% 的价格

turns.en: peers price. But in the subsequent year, you actually see price rise over the many years post the initial entry. The rise of price could be driven by pass on the cost inflation. It could be cyclical factors, but there's also better product, better prices.
turns.zh: 切入市场。但在随后的年份里，你会看到在初次进入市场之后的很多年里，价格其实是上涨的。价格上涨可能是把成本通胀（cost inflation）转嫁出去的结果，也可能是周期性因素，但还有产品更好、因而能卖更好的价钱这一层原因。

turns.en: So if you look at the relative price between Chinese price and their competitor in this market, the discount usually stays quite stable over the period of time. And for example, EV, I think everyone talk about EV, but if you compare the same model Chinese EV versus global, some of the brand names, the discount is around 20%, and it's been
turns.zh: 所以如果你看中国产品与它们在这个市场上的竞争对手之间的相对价格，这个折价幅度在一段时间里通常相当稳定。举个例子，电动车——我想人人都在谈电动车——但如果你拿同一款车型的中国电动车去和全球一些知名品牌比较，折价大约是 20%，而且在

turns.en: very stable in the past three to four years. There is one exception, I always want to mention that is RVC, which is robotic vacuum cleaner you use at home. And this product, when it comes to the US market, came at 40% discount. And today, it's 60% premium, price tripled way faster than this competitor, because
turns.zh: 过去三到四年里一直非常稳定。有一个例外我总想提一提，那就是 RVC，也就是家用的扫地机器人（robotic vacuum cleaner）。这个产品当初进入美国市场时是折价 40% 的，而今天却是溢价（premium）60%，价格涨了三倍，速度远远快过竞争对手，因为

turns.en: it's keep innovating, have all the different functions. If you go to Amazon, you could actually see how impressive it could be. But that's one example of innovation also keeps price higher. So I think it's fair to say the enter of the Chinese product does not necessarily create
turns.zh: 它一直在创新，各种功能都有。你去 Amazon 上看看，就能明白它有多厉害。这就是一个例子：创新同时也把价格撑得更高。所以我觉得可以这么说——中国产品的进入，并不一定会在

turns.en: additional pricing pressure for the many years post the initial entry. But there's a point, as competition carries on. At certain point, we will start to see revenues start coming of companies coming under stress and contraction of revenue or deceleration of growth. That's where we start to see price cut.
turns.zh: 初次进入之后的许多年里带来额外的定价压力。但确实存在一个临界点：随着竞争持续下去，到某个时点，我们会开始看到一些企业的收入承压，出现收入收缩或者增长减速。降价就是从那时候开始的。

turns.en: And these price cut typically are initiated by companies who has been losing market share and trying to defend their market share in a very challenging situation and competition. So the perception that Chinese exports are gaining market share because they're cheaper.
turns.zh: 而这些降价通常是由那些一直在丢市场份额、想要在被动的处境和竞争中守住自身份额的企业率先发起的。所以说，“中国出口靠便宜抢份额”这种看法——

turns.en: If I understand what you're saying correctly, it's true at first, but actually less true over time. And again, if I heard you correctly, product quality ultimately leads a closing of the gap between the price of the Chinese export and the local product. Is that right? That's correct.
turns.zh: 如果我没理解错你的意思，这种看法在一开始是对的，但随着时间推移其实越来越站不住脚。另外，如果我没听错的话，产品质量最终会让中国出口产品与当地产品之间的价格差距收窄。是这样吗？没错。

turns.en: I wouldn't say that's happened to all the products, but we definitely see number of products present themselves in the history that way. And so then we think about the incumbents that are competing against these Chinese exports. Some of them have done a better job than others about hanging on to market share as you just alluded to.
turns.zh: 我不会说所有产品都是这样，但我们确实看到不少产品在历史上就是这么走过来的。那我们再来看看那些与中国出口正面竞争的在位企业（incumbents）。正如你刚才提到的，其中有些企业在守住市场份额这件事上做得比别人好。

turns.en: What makes incumbents more competitive and able to do that and what makes some of them less able to do it? Yes, we see the product nature matters. If you look at the product that is more modular, B2C or high growth, then you tend to see very fast market share game by Chinese companies.
turns.zh: 是什么让某些在位企业更有竞争力、守得住份额，又是什么让另一些守不住？是的，我们认为产品本身的属性很关键。如果看那些更模块化（modular）、面向消费者（B2C）或者高增长的产品，你往往会看到中国企业非常快地抢占市场份额。

turns.en: But on the other hand, if you look at a product that is more interconnected, B2B, more mature, and you tend to see they take a lot longer actually to gain market share, or they tend to be more formidable for the local incumbents. Now in trend with this, we think it's a competitive more entry barrier for these products or segments.
turns.zh: 但反过来，如果看那些关联性更强、面向企业（B2B）、更成熟的产品，你往往会发现它们抢占份额其实要花长得多的时间，或者说当地的在位者对这些中国企业而言更难对付。与此紧密相关的是，我们认为这些产品或细分领域拥有竞争护城河（competitive moat）式的进入壁垒（entry barrier），

turns.en: And it has to build on a very complex interconnected network, for example, service maintenance for full-life cycle for industrial robots. And you could also have these highly complex and the fixed cost-intensive global network for express service such as TDI and local offline channel matters.
turns.zh: 它必须建立在非常复杂、彼此交织的网络之上，比如工业机器人（industrial robots）的全生命周期（full life cycle）服务与维护。快递服务也一样，需要 TDI 那样高度复杂、固定成本密集（fixed-cost-intensive）的全球网络；本地线下渠道同样重要，

turns.en: That's also very valuable and the most important long-term track record where you could have built customer trust and the belief in your products. I think these are the things that takes a very long time to build, therefore I think takes a lot more to compete.
turns.zh: 而且非常有价值。最重要的还是长期的业绩记录（track record）——你借此建立起客户对你产品的信任和信心。我认为这些东西需要非常长的时间才能积累起来，因此要与之竞争，门槛也就高得多。

turns.en: If you think about those factors, are there particular regions or sectors or industries that are especially vulnerable to rising Chinese competition? So the first thing come to mind is industrial segment because this is where Chinese company has built a lot of competitive strengths over the past years.
turns.zh: 如果把这些因素都考虑进去，有没有哪些地区、板块或行业特别容易被不断上升的中国竞争冲击？首先想到的是工业板块（industrial segment），因为过去这些年中国企业正是在这里积累了大量竞争优势。

turns.en: So within that, you could see the early achievers, companies or sectors who already have built strengths in competition and on track with continued market share gain. And I would say these are white goods, electric vehicles, but also keep in mind of the sectors
turns.zh: 在这个板块内部，你能看到一批“先行者”（early achievers）——那些已经在竞争中建立起优势、并且正在持续抢占市场份额的企业或行业。我会说，这些就是白色家电、电动汽车；但同时也要留意那些

turns.en: that new competition from China rising in the sectors, what we call late commerce. And these are, for example, robot-taxi medical equipment, such as surgical robot. You could also see power equipment in transformer and these are old examples. Now there is also another segment that I would probably categorize as outside industrial
turns.zh: 来自中国的竞争刚刚兴起、我们称之为“后来者”（latecomers）的行业。比如说无人驾驶出租车（robotaxi）、手术机器人这类医疗设备，还有变压器所在的电力设备行业，这些都是例子。另外还有一个板块，我大概会把它归到工业之外，

turns.en: that is servicing. And I would say worse monitoring, for example, e-commerce. And on top of that, our analyst has been writing this year a big scene in terms of drug discovery, some of the AI related sector, also worse looking into. And you actually describe some of this expansion through really this lens of disruptive innovation.
turns.zh: 那就是服务业。我觉得值得关注（worth monitoring）的比如电商。除此之外，我们的分析师今年一直在写药物发现（drug discovery）这个大主题；一些与 AI 相关的领域同样值得研究。你其实是用颠覆式创新（disruptive innovation）这个视角来描述其中一部分扩张的。

turns.en: I think you touched on that a little bit already in our conversation, but what does that really mean to you and why is that working so well? Yeah, I was quite amazed when we first started to match this theory developed by Professor Christensen in the 90s and with the Chinese competition coming to go global cases.
turns.zh: 我想你在前面的谈话里已经稍微提到过一点了，但这对你来说究竟意味着什么？为什么它这么奏效？是啊，当我们第一次把 Christensen 教授在上世纪 90 年代提出的这套理论，与中国企业出海参与竞争的案例对上号时，我也相当惊叹。

turns.en: And it's a classic case what the theory is describing about, but there's I think two aspects. One is for Chinese companies, so you wonder why do they succeed when they come into this market initially? The fact is, as described in this theory, Chinese companies, many of them, not all many
turns.zh: 这正是该理论所描述的经典案例。不过我认为有两个层面。一个是中国企业这一侧：你会好奇，为什么它们刚进入这个市场时就能成功？事实是，正如这套理论所描述的那样，中国企业——很多家，不是全部，很多家——

turns.en: of them, they enter the market in the segment that is underserved by established incumbents. And these are basically places also the allocation of resources of incumbents has been also relatively lean because this is not their focus. So you essentially are competing in asymmetrical environment and therefore you have high odds of success.
turns.zh: 进入的是那些成熟的在位企业服务不足（underserved）的细分领域。而这些地方基本上也是在位者资源配置相对薄弱的环节，因为这不是他们的重点。所以你本质上是在一种不对称（asymmetrical）的环境里竞争，成功的概率自然就高。

turns.en: So that actually perfectly described by this theory. But I saw that the other side of this theory with service is probably even more to the large established global companies who's facing the Chinese competition. Quite often when we were doing a study looking at different products and sectors, we hear
turns.zh: 这一点其实被这套理论完美地描述了出来。但我看到，这套理论的另一面，或许更是说给那些正面对中国竞争的大型成熟全球公司听的。我们在研究不同产品和行业时，经常听到

turns.en: dismissive, we hear retreat, let them have the commodity market. Let's us focus on what's most profitable, our best customer and our best market. This is logically right, however, as highlighted in the theory, it also can be very deceptive. And delay your strategic response to the competition.
turns.zh: 不屑一顾的态度，也听到退让：“让他们去做同质化商品（commodity）市场吧，我们专注最赚钱的部分、最好的客户和最好的市场。”这在逻辑上没错；然而正如理论所强调的，它也可能极具迷惑性，让你对竞争的战略回应一拖再拖。

turns.en: So in other words, if you see companies see the peripheral market or the low end segment, they essentially are give the beach head to the competitors Chinese competition and let them have the opportunity to move forward from there to the upper market. So you increase the risk in the future.
turns.zh: 换句话说，如果你看到企业把边缘市场或低端细分拱手让人（cede），它们实际上就是把滩头阵地（beachhead）交给了竞争对手，也就是中国竞争者，让他们有机会从这里向上游市场推进。这样一来，你其实是在放大未来的风险。

turns.en: So it's a function of both the decisions and the opportunities the Chinese companies are pursuing and the response of the income themselves, fascinating. So when you take a step back and you think about this expansion that's occurring, how much do this is actually priced into markets?
turns.zh: 所以这既取决于中国企业追求的机会和做出的决策，也取决于在位者自身的反应。很有意思。那么，当你退一步来看正在发生的这场扩张，市场究竟在多大程度上已经把它计入价格（priced in）了？

turns.en: I would say we look at all the market cap responses to the changing of market share, the revenue. The first I think observation was very clear that market never hesitated at all for companies holding the process of losing their market shares. And the penalties, actually I would describe it as ruthless, for 10 to 15% market share
turns.zh: 我会说，我们观察了市值（market cap）对市场份额和收入变化的反应。第一个观察非常清楚：对于那些正在丢份额的公司，市场从来没有半点犹豫。而这种惩罚，我甚至愿意用“冷酷无情”（ruthless）来形容——失去 10% 到 15% 的

turns.en: loss or top line contraction, the market cap could shrink by 50%, 70%, 80%. So multiples earnings all come together. However, on the other side, it's also very interesting market is very skeptical in giving credit to Chinese companies, this great global ambition.
turns.zh: 市场份额，或者营收（top line）收缩，市值可能缩水 50%、70%、80%。估值倍数和盈利一起往下走。不过在另一侧，也很有意思：市场对于认可中国企业的这份宏大全球抱负，是非常怀疑的。

turns.en: So if you look at the valuation price to sales as today's valuation on say 2035, how much sales these companies are targeted for in today's value, you would have to see a lot of one times, even less than one times, which actually tells you market is worried about these expansions or skeptical about these expansions.
turns.zh: 如果你用市销率（price to sales）来看估值——拿今天的估值去除以比如说 2035 年这些公司被期望达到的销售额——你会看到大量的一倍左右，甚至不到一倍。这实际上说明，市场对这些扩张是担忧的，或者说持怀疑态度。

turns.en: Is that just though a reflection of the market's view of the opportunities of these companies, or does it also relate to the investor base? Who is owning Chinese companies if we put a global lens on that? I think market wants to look for profitable expansions.
turns.zh: 不过，这只是市场对这类企业机会的看法的反映，还是也跟投资者结构（investor base）有关？如果放在全球视角下看，究竟是谁在持有中国公司？我认为市场想找的是能赚钱的扩张。

turns.en: And I have to say there is a very strong narrative out there in your earlier question in terms of how much price impact these expansions are. Are you just gaining market share, or are you gaining profit? Are you being more profitable? I think that we could see some of the successful examples, but the market probably wanted to
turns.zh: 而且我得说，市场里有一种很强的论调，也就是你刚才那个问题涉及的：这些扩张对价格的影响有多大。你只是在抢市场份额，还是在赚利润？你有没有变得更赚钱？我认为确实能看到一些成功的例子，但市场大概还想

turns.en: see more to be convinced that going forward these expansions does not end up with something similar to evolution, where the price actually gets killed because of competition. The other things I would say is today's uncertainty in geopolitics, the market access,
turns.zh: 看到更多证据，才愿意相信往后这些扩张不会重演类似“内卷”（involution）的局面——价格因为竞争被一路杀下去。另外我要说的是，今天地缘政治、市场准入（market access）方面存在不确定性，

turns.en: the trade frictions, and that's the question I get the most on this work is what do we do, Trina? What do we think about these trade discussions and access restrictions and how do we work around it? And it's very difficult because it's not something in our control.
turns.zh: 还有贸易摩擦（trade frictions）。这也是我在这项研究上被问得最多的问题：“Trina，我们该怎么办？”我们怎么看待这些贸易谈判和准入限制，又该怎么绕开它们？这很难，因为它不在我们能掌控的范围之内。

turns.en: And I tend to think that at least number one, I view these restrictions or hurdles as more of a speed bump. So they could change trajectory, but they don't change the outcome in the long run because the competitor is here. Having said that from practical perspective, you have to avoid, for example, product that's
turns.zh: 我的看法至少是这样：第一，我把这些限制或障碍更多地看作减速带（speed bump）。它们可能改变行进轨迹，但长期看改变不了结果，因为竞争对手已经在这里了。话虽如此，从实际操作角度，你必须避开一些产品，比如

turns.en: related to securities of a lot of countries. For example, if you think about our power equipment analyst, she would be very skeptical that Chinese transformer would ever go to the main grid of power grid in US and Europe for security reason. You could also look at the sectors where the contribution to the economy is very significant
turns.zh: 涉及许多国家国家安全（security）的产品。举个例子，如果去问我们的电力设备分析师，她会非常怀疑中国的变压器出于安全原因能进入美国和欧洲电网的主干网（main grid）。你也可以看看那些对经济贡献非常大的行业，
